name: MUBen
description: Large molecular representation models pre-trained on massive unlabeled data have shown great success in predicting molecular properties. However, these models may tend to overfit the fine-tuning data, resulting in over-confident predictions on test data that fall outside of the training distribution. To address this issue, uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods can be used to improve the models' calibration of predictions. Although many UQ approaches exist, not all of them lead to improved performance. While some studies have included UQ to improve molecular pre-trained models, the process of selecting suitable backbone and UQ methods for reliable molecular uncertainty estimation remains underexplored. To address this gap, we present MUBen, which evaluates different UQ methods for state-of-the-art backbone molecular representation models to investigate their capabilities. By fine-tuning various backbones using different molecular descriptors as inputs with UQ methods from different categories, we assess the influence of architectural decisions and training strategies. Our study offers insights for selecting UQ for backbone models, which can facilitate research on uncertainty-critical applications in fields such as materials science and drug discovery.
evaluation_method: negative_log_likelihood (NLL), RMSE/AUROC for predictive performance and calibration metrics such as expected calibration error (ECE) for uncertainty quantification
reputation: A recent research benchmark (arXiv:2306.10060) used in molecular ML and cheminformatics communities to evaluate uncertainty quantification methods; adopted primarily in academic research.
notes: Non-LLM benchmark focused on molecular property prediction and uncertainty; performance depends heavily on backbone and UQ method. May include small or task-specific datasets and is intended for research on calibration and reliable uncertainty estimation.
